scope: WHAT THIS MANIFEST IS FOR: ARTIFACT INTEGRITY. It answers one question -- has a committed file changed since these hashes were recorded -- for the generator, every input read and every figure written. That is what --verify checks and it is all --verify checks. WHAT IT IS NOT: it is NOT a claim that another machine will reproduce these bytes. Three claims are distinct and only the first is made here. (1) BYTE IDENTITY: the same bytes. Asserted only within the RECORDED TEST ENVIRONMENT listed in 'environment' below -- recorded, NOT pinned: this package ships no lockfile and enforces no version check, so that list is a description of what produced these bytes, not a guarantee that reinstalling it reproduces them. The self-test demonstrates it by saving one figure twice in one process. (2) PIXEL IDENTITY: the same rendered image, possibly different bytes. NOT established -- a different FreeType rasterises glyphs differently. (3) CONTENT EQUALITY: the same numbers, labels and marks, possibly different pixels. NOT established by any hash; it is what a reader checks by looking at the figure. A hash mismatch on another machine therefore means 'these bytes differ', not 'this figure is stale' -- read the recorded environment before concluding anything has drifted.

provenance_history.why: No file with the previous hash exists anywhere reachable, so that recorded input had become uncheckable. The replayed panel from the 2026-09-14 reproducibility run was substituted only after a control run at unchanged generator code reproduced all fourteen committed figure files and both derived tables byte-for-byte. SCOPE: that control covered make_figures.py only. The two panels cannot be compared field by field because one no longer exists, so PANEL EQUIVALENCE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. See DATA_AVAILABILITY.md.

note: PDF /CreationDate is frozen to source_date_epoch so figure hashes are meaningful; staleness is detected by the hashes below, not by file times. `generator` is this file: a change to the drawing code with stale figures fails --verify, which input and output hashes alone cannot catch. Regenerate with make_figures.py and compare with --verify. SCOPE: figure hashes are reproducible within the recorded test environment recorded in `environment` above, not across environments; a different freetype or matplotlib can change the bytes and even the pixels, which is a separate claim this manifest does not make.
